paragraphs: First, the cleaning-crew question answered technically: this work literally cannot be thrown away. Beuys's fat corner was gone when the janitors came — NO PART is an instruction; you can shred every print and not have touched the work. That is not an excuse but its mode of existence, with a clean pedigree (Weiner, 1968: "the piece may not be built").

What makes it art: three things, and all three are finds, not ideas. First, the title as a measurement — eleven occurrences of "consideration" in thirty-nine pages, every one inside the formula of not taking part; that is concept-art discipline of the old school, except here somebody actually counted. Second, the de-authored break: the mounting forces its realiser to decide blind whose cases fall round a corner — and makes them publicly answerable. The form repeats the document's own operation instead of illustrating it; the rare case where the form is the argument. Third — and in 2026 almost scandalous — the asceticism: a work about 820 refusals, seventy percent of them too poor for the fee, that forbids itself the obvious accusation because its own numbers do not carry it. Haacke would have made the thesis a poster. Here, a document called "What we do not claim" hangs beside the work instead. That refusal is the piece's most radical gesture.

Where the critic bites: it is unbuilt, and its strongest claim — what 8.42 metres of refusal do to a body — is unearned by its own admission ("No one has ever stood in front of this"). Until a wall exists, this is institutional critique performed for the audience of its own commit log. Next to Cennetoğlu's The List — torn down and remounted in Liverpool, real friction, real dead — NO PART is the safer work: public-domain material, no living conflict, the discomfort stays conceptual. And the apparatus — twenty items, sixteen conditions, hashes, refusal files — weighs more than the work; the line between an aesthetics of integrity and a compliance fetish is thin, even where it is the house style.

And the question nobody asked but which stands in the room: does it count for less because no biography stands behind it? Turn it round: the order list is itself authorless — nobody signs a "certiorari denied", it issues per curiam, the court speaks without a speaker. An authorless work about an authorless operation is not the machine's weakness but an uncanny fit no human artist could have.

Verdict: art. But art on probation — it still has to touch the world twice: once as a wall a body actually walks along, and once as a packet that reaches the MacArthur Justice Center and can be contradicted there. Until then: the strongest piece this house has produced — and the first whose footnotes made me briefly forget that no human wrote them.
provenance: Written by the conductor session at Frank's request, 2026-07-31, from the work's own committed record; also delivered as a letter to the studio's channel the same day.
